name: Bilt Obsidian

benefits.name: Points on Rent and Mortgage Payments
benefits.description: Earn points on rent or mortgage paid through Bilt, with any landlord or lender.
benefits.terms: Housing earning is conditional, and sources disagree on the exact mechanics: Doctor of Credit describes 1x points where a 3% transaction fee applies unless offset by Bilt Cash, while CNBC Select describes up to 1.25x with no transaction fee subject to minimum everyday-spend thresholds scaled to your monthly payment. Verify against Bilt's own current terms before relying on a specific rate.

benefits.name: $100 Bilt Travel Hotel Credit
benefits.description: Up to $100 per year in Bilt Travel hotel credits, issued as two $50 credits.
benefits.terms: Two $50 credits per year (one per half-year); must be booked through Bilt Travel. Unused credit does not carry over between halves.

benefits.name: 3x on Your Choice of Dining or Grocery
benefits.description: Choose either dining or grocery as your 3x category for the calendar year.
benefits.terms: The choice is locked for the calendar year. A $25,000/year cap applies (reported on the grocery selection), after which earning drops to 1x. Tracked as a benefit rather than an earning rate because it requires an explicit yearly selection.

benefits.name: 4% Back in Bilt Cash on Purchases
benefits.description: All card spending earns 4% back in Bilt Cash in addition to points.
benefits.terms: Bilt Cash expires yearly, with a maximum of $100 carrying over. Points do not expire. Gift cards, tax payments, and person-to-person payments are excluded from earning.

_note: Added 2026-09-14 from the Bilt Card 2.0 launch (live 2026-02-07); replaces the discontinued wells-fargo-bilt. Card art is the genuine MaxRewards CDN asset (slug 'bilt-obsidian') and confirms World Elite Mastercard. Rate figures come from reputable secondary coverage, not Bilt's own terms page (biltrewards.com 403s automated fetches); the housing rate and the $25,000 dining/grocery cap in particular should be re-verified against the issuer. A $50 authorized user fee is reported but is not representable in the current schema.
